A curiously feather-fringed avian head peers over tall grasses that rise from the plains like waves in an ocean. Th ese lone hunters 
use their height to survey the wide expanse of their domain for spotting prey scampering in the dry stalks, the prowl of larger, more 
fearsome predators, and the brightly colored fruit that grows on the lofty wollopon trees. With a long stride on wide clawed feet, the 
hectatrex bounds over the flat landscape evading predators and chasing down prey with ease, only being caught unaware in the waning 
hours of the setting sun as their sight is not well suited to low light conditions. Th ough often found alone, during the spring season a 
male and female bird will alternate protecting their young, vulnerable chicks that they conceal in grass woven warrens.
Class - Aves • Genus Derived Evolution - Sagittarius • Niche - Generalist Omnivore
Preyed upon by - Draffer, Grahknash, Khanith, Maedrynn, Tyrandroth • Preys on - Axilot, Korruk, Scavick

Encountering With the advantage of its height, the hectatrex 
often spies approaching creatures and quickly responds by 
escaping into the prairies if they deem them hostile. Th ough 
skittish, these birds do have a curious streak and, if a Traveler 
stands still in the open fi elds holding aloft a vibrant wollopon 
berry, they may turn back and investigate the gift. Th ough be 
wary as the hectatrex can quickly turn violent when threatened. 
Aggressive Instinct (3/day) If the hectatrex suffers damage by an 
enemy creature within 5 ft. of it, and hasn’t used its Reaction this turn.
Reaction - Trigger: A creature the hectatrex can see hits it with an

Success: Th e hectatrex kicks out and attacks. Melee Attack Roll: +6 to 
hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) Bludgeoning damage. If 
the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it is pushed back 5 ft. 
to an unoccupied space.
